title: Cap. V Obj. 3 Sol: Major ambiguous — reject prior existence-as-faithful; grant foresight of what God will make
pass_a_gloss: Solution. The Major has much ambiguity in itself. For if it be taken in that sense, as if every one predestinated to life, antecedently to this decree of predestination, existed of such sort in the Divine intuition as he will be in the very reception of eternal life, it is altogether to be rejected. But if this be the mind of that proposition, When God destinates the elect to life, at the same time from eternity he looks forward, and looks upon of what sort he will make them, before he leads them through to life, and contemplates the same, as such, to be introduced into possession of eternal life, that indeed is most true, and cannot be denied, unless someone wish to deny that God foreknows what he himself is about to do.
pass_b_english: Sol. The Major is highly ambiguous. If it means every one predestinated to life already existed in God's intuition, before the predestination decree, as he will be in receiving eternal life — reject it outright. But if it means: when God destinates the elect to life, he at once from eternity looks ahead and sees of what sort he will make them before leading them to life, and contemplates them as such to be brought into possession of eternal life — that is most true, and cannot be denied unless one denies that God foreknows what he himself will do.
source_text: Sol. Major multum in se habet ambiguitatis. Nam si eo sensu capiatur, quasi omnis ad vitam praedestinatus, antecedenter ad hoc decretum praedestinationis, talis existeret in intuitu Divino, qualis futurus est in ipsa acceptione vitae aeternae, prorsus rejicienda est. Si vero haec sit illius propositionis mens, Quando Deus electos ad vitam destinat, simul ab aeterno prospicit, et intuetur quales sit eos effecturus, antequam ad vitam perducat, eosdemque, ut tales, in vitae aeternae possessionem introducendos contempletur, id quidem verissimum est, nec negari potest, nisi quis negare velit Deum praescire quae ipse est facturus.
